what_happened: The task description's sub-question claimed 'THE AGGREGATOR IS THE SOLE CONSUMER of issues.jsonl', citing skill-todo and skill-learn's explicit self-prohibitions as support. A grep for issues.jsonl across agent-system/extensions/ found a second real consumer: agent-system/extensions/books/scripts/books-observe.sh reads each task's issues.jsonl directly (for by_kind/dimension_signals/tags/burdens joins). The claim is therefore imprecise as stated. The dispatch's bottom-line conclusion ('a filter change has no blast radius outside the conclusion stage') still holds on verification, because books-observe.sh never reads or filters on the .resolution field anywhere in its own script or its observation-record.md/signal-tagging.md docs -- confirmed by grep. Corrected framing: the aggregator is the sole CONSUMER OF THE RESOLUTION FIELD, not the sole reader of the file.

scripts/tests/test-orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh's Case (a) (resolution filtering) exercises open, worked_around, and fixed_inline explicitly but has no case at all for a null/omitted --resolution on a kind:issue entry -- exactly the value that caused the live defect this task exists to fix. A cheap test case asserting null's treatment (currently: silently dropped) would have caught this defect before it reached a live /orchestrate run. Recommending the plan/implement phase add this case regardless of which remedy is chosen, asserting the post-fix behavior explicitly.

The dispatch's evidence enumeration (six specific entry_ids across two BimodalLogic fixture files, plus the one exempted win entry) was verified byte-for-byte against the actual ~/Projects/BimodalLogic/specs/archive/739.../issues.jsonl and 740.../issues.jsonl files -- every entry_id, kind, class, and resolution:null value matched exactly as described, with no corrections needed to that part of the dispatch. Saved a full independent re-derivation of the fixture evidence.

test-orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh resolves its script under test deployed-copy-first (REPO_ROOT/.claude/scripts/... precedes the source-store fallback), so running that suite after a source-store edit but before deploy silently exercises the stale code and reports a false green. Discovered at plan time while choosing per-phase verification tiers; worked around by ordering deploy strictly before any suite run and by declaring the code phases' tiers on lint plus a jq parse only, with an explicit note that they do not claim suite coverage.

The research report's recommendation 5 directed updating the utility-scripts-inventory descriptions of BOTH issue-record.sh and orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh, but a plan-time grep found no aggregator row in that inventory at all (consistent with its stated inclusion criterion excluding lifecycle scripts). Corrected inline by narrowing the plan step to the issue-record.sh row and attaching a Scope Hypothesis that names the grep to re-run and the criterion to re-read.

The aggregator suite's own build_scratch helper turned out to be a reusable recipe for running the mandated BimodalLogic 739/740 regression fixture WITHOUT a cross-repo deploy: copy the deployed script plus its three libs into a scratch .claude tree, write a scratch specs/state.json, and copy the real issues.jsonl files in read-only. This removed the plan's only genuinely risky step (deploying into a second live repo) and let the expected post-fix figures be derived exactly from the real 18 fixture entries at plan time.

validate-state.sh --deep found specs/TODO.md out of sync with specs/state.json (missing a Summary artifact link for task 372) ahead of this task's Phase 4 gate run. Root cause: task 372's completion commit (808776bf3) updated state.json but did not regenerate TODO.md with the final state. Fixed by running bash .claude/scripts/generate-todo.sh, a safe idempotent regeneration unrelated to task 373's own file_scope; the one-line fix is folded into this task's final completion commit rather than a separate out-of-scope commit.

verify-deploy.sh Gate 3 (check-extension-docs.sh) FAILs on core: 'script referenced in docs/skills/agents but NOT in provides.scripts: check-evidence-probes.sh', reproduced identically against this task's own redeployed tree. Confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to task 373's four-file scope (same root cause already filed by a sibling task against skill-todo/SKILL.md and context/patterns/task-abandon-mode.md, both untouched by this task). Excluded from this phase's acceptance per status-markers.md's five-condition test; not refiled as a duplicate.

tests/run-all.sh's full battery reported test-four-tier-conflict.sh case 6 ('budget-bound') FAILing with elapsed_ms~2068-2155 against a budget_ms=1000 ceiling. Reproduced in isolation (outside run-all.sh's parallel battery too), confirming a genuine wall-clock-budget overrun under current system load rather than a run-all.sh parallelism artifact. The failing script (agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/test-four-tier-conflict.sh) exercises task-lock acquire-retry timing, has zero relation to task 373's four-file scope (orchestrate-conclusion-aggregate.sh, its test, issue-log.md, conclusion-stage.md), and was not touched by this task. Two other run-all.sh-reported failures (test-orchestrate-recover-outcome.sh, test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh) were independently re-run in isolation: the former passed cleanly (7/7, a parallel-battery flake); the latter's 'baseline fixture is not clean' failure traces to the SAME pre-existing check-evidence-probes.sh gate-3 defect recorded in a sibling issue entry, reproduced byte-for-byte against the fixture. None of the three is a regression introduced by this task's edits.,evidence_path:agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/test-four-tier-conflict.sh

Append-only discipline applies to this task's own issues.jsonl the same as to any other repo's, so the malformed entry is left as-is rather than hand-edited; this entry supplies the corrected evidence_path for the record: agent-system/extensions/core/scripts/test-four-tier-conflict.sh.
